title: Feelings & opinions
goal: Say how you feel, give your opinion, agree and disagree, and link ideas with 'because', 'but' and 'so'.
intro: Many feelings in Odia work like hunger in Unit 5: they *strike* you (ମୋତେ ଡର ଲାଗୁଛି 'I'm scared'). Others are simple descriptions (ମୁଁ ଖୁସି 'I'm happy'). In this unit you also learn to say **I think that…** and to join sentences with **କାରଣ**, **କିନ୍ତୁ** and **ସେଥିପାଇଁ**.

vocab.note: ମୋତେ ଡର ଲାଗୁଛି 'I'm scared'. Formal: ଭୟ.
ମୋର ପସନ୍ଦ 'my choice / to my liking'.

phrases.en: I felt bad. / That hurt my feelings.

grammar.title: Giving opinions: ମୁଁ ଭାବୁଛି, ମୋତେ ଲାଗୁଛି, ମୋ ମତରେ
grammar.body:
Three common ways to introduce an opinion:
**ମୁଁ ଭାବୁଛି (ଯେ) …** 'I think (that) …' — ଯେ is optional in speech.
**ମୋତେ ଲାଗୁଛି (ଯେ) …** 'it seems to me …' — dative, very common.
**ମୋ ମତରେ …** 'in my opinion …'.

The clause after ଯେ is a normal sentence with the verb at the end. To agree: **ମୁଁ ରାଜି**, **ଠିକ୍ କହୁଛ / କହୁଛନ୍ତି** 'you're right', **ସତ କଥା** 'true'. To disagree politely: **ମୁଁ ରାଜି ନୁହେଁ** 'I don't agree', **ମୋତେ ସେମିତି ଲାଗୁନି** 'I don't think so'.

examples.native: ମୋ ମତରେ ଏ ଫିଲ୍ମଟି ଭଲ ନୁହେଁ।
examples.roman: mo môtôre e philmôṭi bhôlô nuheṃ.
examples.en: In my opinion this film isn't good.

grammar.title: Linking ideas: and, but, because, so, or
grammar.body:
**ଓ / ଆଉ / ଏବଂ** 'and' (ଏବଂ is formal) · **କିନ୍ତୁ** 'but' · **କାରଣ** 'because' · **ସେଥିପାଇଁ / ତେଣୁ** 'so, that's why' · **କି / ନା** 'or' (ନା mostly in questions: ଚା ନା କଫି? 'tea or coffee?') · **ଯଦିଓ** 'although'.

These go between two full clauses, just as in English. A very Odia alternative to କାରଣ is the verb in **-ବାରୁ** ('because of …ing'), placed first: ବର୍ଷା ହେବାରୁ … 'because it rained …'.

examples.en: I'm happy because today's a holiday.
I'm tired, so I'll stay at home.
The film is long, but fun.
Because it rained, we couldn't go.

dialogue.title: Talking about a film
dialogue.setting: Bapi and Sam discuss a new Odia film at a tea stall.

lines.speaker: Bapi
lines.en: Sam, have you seen the new Odia film?

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.native: ହଁ, ଦେଖିଛି। ମୋତେ ବହୁତ ଭଲ ଲାଗିଲା।
lines.roman: hôṃ, dekhichhi. mote bôhutô bhôlô lagila.
lines.en: Yes, I have. I really liked it.

lines.speaker: Bapi
lines.native: ସତରେ? ମୁଁ ଭାବୁଥିଲି ତୁମେ ସବୁ ବୁଝିପାରିବ ନାହିଁ।
lines.roman: sôtôre? muṃ bhabuthili tume sôbu bujhiparibô nahiṃ.
lines.en: Really? I thought you wouldn't understand it all.

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.native: ସବୁ ବୁଝିଲି ନାହିଁ, କିନ୍ତୁ ଗୀତଗୁଡ଼ିକ ଭାରି ସୁନ୍ଦର।
lines.roman: sôbu bujhili nahiṃ, kintu gitôguṛikô bhari sundôrô.
lines.en: I didn't understand everything, but the songs are lovely.

lines.speaker: Bapi
lines.en: In my opinion the story is a bit weak.

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.native: ମୁଁ ରାଜି ନୁହେଁ। ମୋତେ ଲାଗୁଛି କାହାଣୀଟି ଭଲ, କେବଳ ଶେଷ ଟିକେ ଲମ୍ବା।
lines.roman: muṃ raji nuheṃ. mote laguchhi kahaṇiṭi bhôlô, kebôḷô sesô ṭike lômba.
lines.en: I don't agree. I think the story is good, only the ending is a bit long.

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.native: ତୁମକୁ କେଉଁ ପ୍ରକାର ଫିଲ୍ମ ଭଲ ଲାଗେ?
lines.roman: tumôku keuṃ prôkarô philmô bhôlô lage?
lines.en: What kind of films do you like?

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.native: ତେବେ ପରଥର ଆମେ ଏକାଠି କମେଡି ଦେଖିବା।
lines.roman: tebe pôrôthôrô ame ekaṭhi kômeḍi dekhiba.
lines.en: Then next time we'll watch a comedy together.

culture: Odias tend to express disagreement gently — with *hôu* ('okay…'), a smile or 'ଦେଖିବା' ('we'll see') — rather than a flat 'no', especially with elders. Odia cinema (*Ollywood*, based in Cuttack and Bhubaneswar) and especially Odia film and *bhajan* songs are a big part of popular culture, as is *jatra*, the travelling folk theatre.

tip.title: ମୁଁ ଖୁସି but ମୋତେ ଡର ଲାଗୁଛି
tip.body:
- Some feelings are simply what you *are*: **ମୁଁ** ଖୁସି 'I'm happy', ମୁଁ ଦୁଃଖୀ 'I'm sad'.
- Others *strike* you, so the person takes **-କୁ / ମୋତେ**: **ମୋତେ** ଡର ଲାଗୁଛି 'I'm scared', ମୋତେ ଲାଜ ଲାଗୁଛି 'I feel shy'.
- ତୁମେ → **ତୁମକୁ**, ସେ → **ତାଙ୍କୁ**, ପିଲାଟି → **ପିଲାଟିକୁ**.

sentences.en: I feel a bit shy.
I'm very sad today.
The child is scared.

sentences.native: ସେ ଏକୁଟିଆ ରହନ୍ତି, ତାଙ୍କୁ ଏକୁଟିଆ ଲାଗେ।
sentences.roman: se ekuṭia rôhônti, taṅku ekuṭia lage.
sentences.en: She lives alone and feels lonely.
Are you scared?
No, I'm happy. And you?
He is very unhappy. (lit. he has much sorrow)

sentences.native: ଏକୁଟିଆ ଯାଅ ନାହିଁ, ମୁଁ ବି ଆସୁଛି।
sentences.roman: ekuṭia jaô nahiṃ, muṃ bi asuchhi.
sentences.en: Don't go alone — I'm coming too.

lessons.title: Tired, angry and fed up — and why

tip.title: But, because, so
tip.body:
- **କିନ୍ତୁ** 'but' · **କାରଣ** 'because' · **ସେଥିପାଇଁ / ତେଣୁ** 'so, that's why'.
- They sit between two full sentences, just like in English: ମୁଁ କ୍ଲାନ୍ତ, **କିନ୍ତୁ** ଖୁସି.
- Watch the direction: **କାରଣ** + the reason; **ସେଥିପାଇଁ** + the result.

sentences.native: ମୁଁ ଥକି ଯାଇଛି, କାରଣ ସବୁଦିନ ଡେରିରେ ଶୁଏ।
sentences.roman: muṃ thôki jaichhi, karôṇô sôbudinô ḍerire sue.
sentences.en: I'm tired because I go to bed late every day.

sentences.native: ସେ ରାଗିଛନ୍ତି, ସେଥିପାଇଁ କିଛି କହୁ ନାହାନ୍ତି।
sentences.roman: se ragichhônti, sethipaiṃ kichhi kôhu nahanti.
sentences.en: He's angry — that's why he isn't saying anything.
I'm tired, but happy.
She's fed up, so she's going home.
The train's late, so I'm fed up.

sentences.native: ମୁଁ ଆଜି ଖୁସି, କାରଣ ମୋ ସାଙ୍ଗ ଆସୁଛି।
sentences.roman: muṃ aji khusi, karôṇô mo saṅgô asuchhi.
sentences.en: I'm happy today because my friend is coming.
He's angry with me.
Please don't be angry — I'm sorry.

tip.title: I think (that) …
tip.body:
- **ମୁଁ ଭାବୁଛି (ଯେ) …** 'I think (that) …' — ଯେ can be left out.
- **ମୋତେ ଲାଗୁଛି …** 'it seems to me …' (very common).
- **ମୋ ମତରେ …** 'in my opinion …'.
- After ଯେ comes a normal sentence, verb last. ଭାବିବା changes with the person: ମୁଁ ଭାବୁଛି, ତୁମେ ଭାବୁଛ, ସେ ଭାବୁଛନ୍ତି.

sentences.native: ମୁଁ ଭାବୁଛି ଯେ ଏହି ହୋଟେଲ ଭଲ।
sentences.roman: muṃ bhabuchhi je ehi hoṭelô bhôlô.
sentences.en: I think this hotel is good.
I think it's going to rain.

sentences.native: ମୋ ମତରେ ଓଡ଼ିଆ ଭାଷା ବହୁତ ସୁନ୍ଦର।
sentences.roman: mo môtôre Oṛia bhasa bôhutô sundôrô.
sentences.en: In my opinion Odia is a beautiful language.
What do you think?

sentences.native: ମୋତେ ଲାଗୁଛି ଯେ ଟ୍ରେନ୍ ଡେରି ହେବ।
sentences.roman: mote laguchhi je ṭren ḍeri hebô.
sentences.en: I think the train will be late.

sentences.native: ବାପା ଭାବୁଛନ୍ତି ଯେ ମୁଁ ବହୁତ ଟିଭି ଦେଖେ।
sentences.roman: bapa bhabuchhônti je muṃ bôhutô ṭibhi dekhe.
sentences.en: Dad thinks I watch too much TV.
Maybe he won't come today.
She'll definitely come.

sentences.native: ତୁମ ମତ କ'ଣ, ଏଇଟା ନା ସେଇଟା?
sentences.roman: tumô môtô kôṇô, eiṭa na seiṭa?
sentences.en: What do you think — this one or that one?

tip.title: You're right / I don't agree
tip.body:
- Agree: **ମୁଁ ରାଜି** 'I agree', **ଠିକ୍ କହୁଛ** 'you're right' (polite: ଠିକ୍ କହୁଛନ୍ତି), **ସତ କଥା** 'true'.
- Disagree politely: **ମୁଁ ରାଜି ନୁହେଁ** — ନୁହେଁ, not ନାହିଁ, because it's 'am not'.
- Surprised? **ସତରେ?** 'Really?'

sentences.en: I agree with you.
No, I don't agree.
You're right.
You're wrong.
You're right, I agree.
Don't lie!
Really? That's not a lie, is it?
That's my mistake — sorry.
She always tells the truth.
The kids are laughing a lot.
Don't cry — everything will be fine.
We had a lot of fun on the beach.
This isn't really my taste.
Which colour do you like?

sentences.native: ଆଶ୍ଚର୍ଯ୍ୟ କଥା, ସେ ଆଜି ଠିକ୍ ସମୟରେ ଆସିଲେ!
sentences.roman: aschôrjyô kôtha, se aji ṭhik sômôyôre asile!
sentences.en: Amazing — he came on time today!
Don't worry, I'm here. (familiar)

sentences.native: ମୁଁ ଓ ମୋ ଭଉଣୀ ଏକାଠି ବହୁତ ହସୁ।
sentences.roman: muṃ o mo bhôuṇi ekaṭhi bôhutô hôsu.
sentences.en: My sister and I laugh a lot together.

sentences.native: ତାଙ୍କ କଥା ଶୁଣି ମୋତେ ବହୁତ ଖରାପ ଲାଗିଲା।
sentences.roman: taṅkô kôtha suṇi mote bôhutô khôrapô lagila.
sentences.en: What he said really hurt me.
